title: Free Fall: Force, Mass and Acceleration
learningObjectives: Calculate acceleration as net force divided by mass for one-dimensional motion.
Explain that in a vacuum free-fall acceleration is constant and independent of weight, size, and shape.
Predict how velocity and displacement change over time under constant acceleration.

evidence.quote: An object that falls through a vacuum is subjected to only one external force, the gravitational force, expressed as the weight of the object.
its motion is described by Newton’s second law of motion.

explanations.text: In a vacuum an object is pulled only by gravity acting as its weight. Motion caused only by gravity is free fall and is described by Newton's second law of motion.

evidence.quote: The acceleration is constant and equal to the gravitational acceleration g which is 9.8 meters per square second at sea level on the Earth.
In a vacuum, a beach ball falls with the same acceleration as an airliner.

explanations.text: Free-fall acceleration is constant at sea level at 9.8 meters per square second. Weight, size and shape do not matter, so in a vacuum a beach ball and an airliner share the same acceleration.
With constant acceleration, velocity follows V = a * t and displacement follows X = (1 / 2) * a * t^2, allowing velocity and location to be found at any time.

evidence.quote: Notice that the acceleration is a constant, the velocity increases linearly, and the location increases quadratically.

explanations.text: Under constant acceleration, velocity increases linearly with time while location increases quadratically with time.

behavioralTests.name: zero net force gives zero acceleration
